issue.title: canirun.ai doesn't take into account moe offloading to cpu

comment.body:
Implemented and deployed in dbce5d3.

MoE compatibility now:
- keeps the full model footprint for fit, memory usage, and CPU-offload status
- uses active parameters for throughput estimates
- applies a RAM/CPU bandwidth penalty when expert weights do not all fit in VRAM

The active-parameter metadata is now used by the model list, model details, hardware comparison, tier list, public compatibility API, recommendations, and runai.

Production verification with Ornith 1.0 35B-A3B Q4_K_M:
- 24 GB VRAM: comfortable, ~447 t/s
- 12 GB VRAM + 64 GB RAM: cpu-offload, ~50 t/s

Regression cases were added but not executed because this repository's AGENTS.md asks agents not to run tests/typecheck/lint unless explicitly requested.

issue.title: Feature request: Add a compatibility API for deployed instances
issue.body:
## Feature request

Hi ??

First of all, thanks for the project - CanIRun.ai is really useful for quickly checking whether a machine can run local AI models.

I would like to suggest adding an API endpoint that could be used when the application is deployed, allowing external tools or services to query model compatibility programmatically.

## Use case

Today, the application is very useful through the web UI, but it would also be valuable to expose the same compatibility logic through an API.

For example, I would like to send PC hardware characteristics and a target model, then receive a structured response telling me:

- whether the machine can run the model;
- which quantization is recommended;
- estimated VRAM/RAM requirements;
- available memory headroom;
- estimated performance, such as tokens per second;
- compatibility grade or status.

This would make it possible to integrate CanIRun.ai into other tools, dashboards, hardware comparison websites, internal IT tools, or custom assistants.

## Example API

```http
POST /api/compatibility
```

### Example request:
```json
 {
  "hardware": {
    "cpu": {
      "name": "AMD Ryzen 7 5800X",
      "cores": 8,
      "threads": 16
    },
    "ramGb": 32,
    "gpu": {
      "name": "NVIDIA RTX 3060",
      "vramGb": 12,
      "memoryBandwidthGbps": 360
    }
  },
  "modelId": "llama-3.1-8b",
  "quantization": "Q4_K_M"
}
```


Example response:
```json
{
  "compatible": true,
  "status": "comfortable",
  "grade": "A",
  "modelId": "llama-3.1-8b",
  "recommendedQuantization": "Q4_K_M",
  "estimated": {
    "tokensPerSecond": 38,
    "modelSizeGb": 4.5,
    "vramRequiredGb": 5.8,
    "ramRequiredGb": 8.2,
    "memoryHeadroomGb": 6.2
  },
  "notes": [
    "The model should fit comfortably in GPU memory.",
    "Q5_K_M may also be possible depending on context size.",
    "The estimate is based on available VRAM and memory bandwidth."
  ]
}
```

## Other Possible endpoints

A small API could expose endpoints such as:
GET  /api/models
GET  /api/models/:id
POST /api/compatibility
POST /api/recommend

### Where:

/api/models returns the available model catalog.
/api/models/:id returns metadata for one model.
/api/compatibility checks one hardware profile against one model.
/api/recommend returns the best compatible models for a given hardware profile.

## Why this would be useful
This would allow CanIRun.ai to be used not only as a website, but also as a compatibility engine.

Some possible integrations:
- custom dashboards;
- PC configurators;
- local AI recommendation tools;
- enterprise inventory checks;
- CLI tools;
- automated hardware/model matching;
- browser extensions or third-party UIs.

comment.body:
Implemented and deployed in e558f63.

The public API now exposes:

- `GET /api/models`
- `GET /api/models/:id`
- `POST /api/compatibility`
- `POST /api/recommend`

The endpoints are CORS-enabled, validate malformed input, enrich known GPU names from the hardware database, and use the same compatibility engine as the site. Usage examples are documented in the README.

Production: https://canirun.ai/api/models

issue.title: GPU_DB entry test is failing
issue.body:
## Describe the bug
test case "every GPU_DB entry has a valid category" from `hardware.test.ts` is failing

## To Reproduce

launch all test suites
```sh
pnpm test
```

## Expected behavior

All test suites should passes (all green :D)

## Priority
P4
[Reference - Google Issue tracker priority levels](https://developers.google.com/issue-tracker/concepts/issues#priority)

## Screenshots/Video

```sh
Test: hardware.test.ts > GPU_DB integrity > every GPU_DB entry has a valid category
File: file:///Users/birrame.sene/workspace/canirun.ai/tests/hardware.test.ts

AssertionError: expected 'Other' not to be 'Other' // Object.is equality
  at /Users/birrame.sene/workspace/canirun.ai/tests/hardware.test.ts:66:23
```


## Device
 - OS: MacOS Tahoe 26.5.2
- Model: Macbook M1 Pro 32GB

## Root cause analysis


`getGPUCategory` at line 1462 of `packages/compatibility/src/index.ts` lacks a pattern for Tesla-branded GPUs. Here the mechanism

 ```ts
   export function getGPUCategory(name: string): string {
     // Pro/workstation cards must be checked BEFORE consumer series (e.g. "RTX 5000 Ada" vs "RTX 5090")
     ....

     if (/^(A100|H100|GH200|DGX Spark|L40S|L4|T4|Tesla P40)$/.test(name)).           // missing Testla V100 here
       return "NVIDIA Datacenter";                                                      

     ...
 ```
